The model is not your bottleneck. Your organization is.

Stanford researchers studied 51 enterprise AI deployments across seven countries, nine industries, and 14 business functions. Their finding should reframe every AI investment conversation in the C-suite: in 42% of cases, the AI model itself was wholly interchangeable.

The actual barriers to AI success were process redesign, team trust, organizational understanding, and data infrastructure. Not the technology. Not the model. Not the parameters.

This validates what high-performing AI teams already know — the difference between a pilot and a production system is not a better model. It is a better operating model. Strategy, change management, data architecture, and cross-functional alignment are where value is created or destroyed.

Executives spending disproportionate time evaluating GPT-5.5 versus Claude Opus 4.6 versus Gemini 3.1 Ultra are optimizing the wrong variable. The model layer is converging. The execution layer is diverging — and that is where competitive advantage lives.
